deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is part of a set of German notes on ancient history, probably lecture or reading notes; the hand and purpose are not established here. The section is headed on the previous page '2) Geschichte des Aegyptischen Reichs unter den Ptolemaeern 323–30 a.c.', and this page covers Ptolemy I Soter. Its content, in order:

(1) Ptolemy son of Lagus (Soter), founder of the dynasty, received Egypt as governor (satrap) in 323 BC.
(2) He extended his holdings in Africa, becoming master of Cyrene in 321. Cyrene stayed with Egypt, with some interruptions, and Marmarica also came under Egyptian rule.
(3) In Asia he took part of Syria and Phoenicia. The notes call this region the 'bulwark' (Vormauer) of Egypt, without which he could have no sea power. He also acquired Cyprus.
(4) He took the royal title in 307 (as written).
(5) 'We do not know what conditions were like in Egypt itself.' He was 'one of the greatest princes'.
(6) He reigned 40 years and died in 284 (as written).
(7) His (probably second) wife Berenice persuaded him to make her son his successor, who followed as Ptolemy II. The next page continues with Philadelphus 284–246.

There are no derivations, formulas or computations. The only numbers are dates BC. The one implicit arithmetic is reign length: 323 − 284 = 39, i.e. about 40 years.
errors: Historical: the royal title is usually dated 306/305 BC (formal assumption c. 305/304), not 307.
Historical: Ptolemy I made Ptolemy II co-regent in 285/284 and died in 283/282 BC. '†284' conflates abdication or co-regency with death. 'Regierte 40 Jahr' is a round figure (323–284 = 39 years).
Not an error on this page, but in context: the next page's '33000 Städte' echoes Theocritus' poetic figure of 33,333 cities. It is a traditional exaggeration, not a fact.

results.what: Chronological summary of Ptolemy I Soter's career: satrapy 323, Cyrene 321, Coele-Syria/Phoenicia and Cyprus, royal title, succession of Ptolemy II
results.modern_name: Hellenistic history (Ptolemaic Egypt); standard textbook content, e.g. in the style of Göttingen history lectures such as Heeren's
results.usually_credited_to: Ancient sources (Diodorus, Pausanias, Justin) via 18th/19th-century historical handbooks

deep.surprise_reason: The page is non-mathematical history notes copying standard textbook chronology of the Ptolemies. Nothing on it bears on Gauss's mathematics, and it may not even be in his hand.

checkable.asserts: The reign from 323 to 284 BC spans 39 years, consistent with the rounded 'regierte 40 Jahr'.
The dates for Philadelphus given on the next page (284–246) imply a 38-year reign.

transcription_corrections: Line 'Seine[?] Gemahlin Berenice': the image appears to show a numeral before 'Gemahlin', likely 'Seine 2te Gemahlin Berenice' (Berenice was indeed Ptolemy I's later wife, after Eurydice).
'zum Nachfolger zu machen[?]': 'machen' is confirmed; it is written cramped at the line end.
Otherwise the machine transcription agrees with the image (Lagi Soter, Gouverneur, Cyrene 321, Marmarica, Vormauer, Cyprus, 307, †284).
